_comment: Hand-written fixture corpus for scripts/evaluate_research.py. Three things
are measured against it: whether an admitted follow-up chip points at a
passage that can actually answer it, whether the debate classifier tells a
two-sided question from a one-sided one, and whether a published page's
drift check reports exactly the passages that changed.
THE TRAPS ARE THE POINT. A corpus the harness cannot fail measures nothing
— the mistake evaluate_retrieval.py was rebuilt to undo. Two are planted
here deliberately:
1. 'the Best Practices doc' contains the word 'best' inside a proper noun
and MUST classify plain. Space-padding does NOT save it — 'the Best
Practices doc' really does contain ' best ' — so this trap is what took
the superlatives out of DEBATE_MARKERS entirely. Every marker left is a
comparative, which does not turn up inside proper nouns.
2. 'Do we keep Postgres or move to DuckDB' is genuinely two-sided and
carries no marker word at all, so it classifies PLAIN. That is a known
limit of a pure word test, recorded here rather than pretended away: the
alternative is a model-written classifier, which would inherit exactly
the one-sidedness the counter-evidence pass exists to catch. Its label
below is therefore 'plain' — the label records what the classifier
should say, and the limit is named in this comment.

documents.text:
# Retention policy

The retention window for raw event logs is ninety days. After ninety days the rows are aggregated into daily rollups and the raw rows are deleted. Finance asked for a longer window for billing events, so billing events are kept for seven years in a separate archive bucket.

The archive bucket is write-once. Nothing in the product deletes from it, and a deletion request is handled by a manual runbook that the compliance team owns.

# Storage engines

Postgres is the primary store for every transactional table. It handles the workspace's own rows, the run ledger and the audit trail, and it is the only store that is backed up hourly.

DuckDB is used for the analytics path only. It reads Parquet extracts and answers dashboard queries, and it holds no durable state of its own. A DuckDB file lost is a file we can rebuild from the extracts.

# Best Practices doc

The Best Practices doc collects the conventions this team has agreed to. It covers naming, migration guards, and how a scoped resource is deleted.

The convention for deletion is that contents go with their container. A space's sources and memories are deleted with the space rather than relabelled, because relabelling them would widen what they are retrievable from.

# On-call rotation

The on-call rotation runs weekly and hands over on Monday morning. The primary handles pages; the secondary handles escalations and anything the primary cannot reach within fifteen minutes.

Paging thresholds are reviewed each quarter. The last review moved the error-rate threshold from two percent to one percent.
